w:r.w:t: Provider Today Live Refresh and Shared JavaScript
User Manual / Technical Guide
Project: FastQ Manager Web
Date: June 10, 2026
Audience: Developers and support users who maintain Provider Today and Provider Calendar.
Purpose

This manual explains how the Provider Today live refresh works, why Priscilla's partial refresh was losing button behavior, how shared JavaScript fixes the issue, and how notifications are generated when another application inserts or updates appointments and walk-ins.

High-Level Flowchart
What Was Wrong Before

Priscilla added a partial view to reload walk-ins. The partial refresh replaced the existing table HTML. That removed the old DOM elements, including the buttons that already had JavaScript behavior attached.
The old approach attached events directly to individual buttons:
button.addEventListener("click", function () { ... });
When the partial refresh inserted new buttons, those new buttons did not automatically receive the old handlers or disabled/enabled state calculations.
- Rows could appear correctly but buttons could stop responding.
- Buttons could lose greyed-out/disabled state.
- Meeting Info and expandable text could lose click behavior after refresh.
The Fix: Delegated Event Handling
The shared script now listens once at document level. Clicks bubble up from the clicked element to document. The handler then checks whether the click came from a supported target.
document.addEventListener("click", function (event) { var button = event.target.closest("[data-provider-action]"); if (!button) return; });
Because document is not replaced during partial refresh, newly inserted buttons continue to work.
Shared selectors handled by provider-common.js:
- [data-provider-action] for Check-In, Start, End, Transfer, Cancel.
- .meeting-link for Info / Meeting Details.
- .expandable-text for long queue/service/reference values.
- .accordion-toggle[data-target] for expanding row detail actions.
How provider-common.js Is Loaded
Today.cshtml loads the script at line 286. Calendar.cshtml loads it at line 235.
<script src="@Url.Content("~/Scripts/provider-common.js?v=20260607-1")"></script>
The version query string prevents the browser from serving an older cached copy.
How Pages Call Common JS
Each page reads the shared object:
var providerCommon = window.FastQProviderCommon;
Today.cshtml line 342 and Calendar.cshtml line 313 create this local reference. The pages then call shared functions while still passing page-specific rules.

providerCommon.bindProviderActionButtons({ canAction: canAction, getStatusForAppointment: getStatusForAppointment, openRouteModal: openRouteModal, openEndServiceModal: openEndServiceModal, openCancelServiceModal: openCancelServiceModal, postForm: postForm, providerActionUrl: providerActionUrl, queueLiveSync: queueLiveSync });
Important point: provider-common.js handles DOM mechanics. Today.cshtml and Calendar.cshtml still own business rules such as whether an action is allowed.
Action Button State
The shared script recalculates disabled/enabled state in provider-common.js line 139. It loops through current buttons at line 145.
button.disabled = !canAction(status, action, queueId, getRowDate(button));
The canAction function stays page-specific. This keeps business rules close to each page while avoiding duplicate DOM event code.
Rules currently include:
- Check-In is allowed only for Scheduled.
- Start is allowed for Scheduled or Arrived.
- End is allowed only for InService.
- Transfer is blocked while InService.
- Cancel is blocked while InService or finished.
- Queue permission is also checked.
30-Second Refresh Behavior
Today.cshtml starts the timer at line 3505:
setInterval(refreshExternalProviderRows, 30 * 1000);
Every 30 seconds it calls refreshExternalProviderRows at line 3496.
There are two refresh paths.
Path A: Appointments are visible
When appointments are visible, Today uses full table sync:
queueLiveSync(true);
This is called at Today.cshtml line 3498. The true flag means notifications should be created for detected external changes.
queueLiveSync starts at line 2634 and calls syncTablesFromServer at line 2640.
syncTablesFromServer starts at line 2570. It fetches the current Provider Today page HTML in the background, parses it, and compares the returned table rows with the current table rows.
Important: the UI does not visually reload the whole page. The browser fetches a current server-rendered snapshot, then JavaScript inserts/replaces/removes row pairs in the existing DOM.
Path B: Only walk-ins are visible
When only walk-ins are visible, Today uses the lighter partial refresh:
refreshWalkinsPartial();
This is called at Today.cshtml line 3502. The function starts at line 3458.
It calls Provider/ReloadWalkins and replaces only #partialWalkinsContainer.
How Row Changes Are Detected
Today takes a snapshot before and after refresh.
Snapshot function starts at Today.cshtml line 2447:
getProviderRowSnapshot(root)
Comparison function starts at line 2467:
collectProviderRowChanges(before, after)
Full table sync applies incoming rows in applyIncomingRows, which starts at line 2511. It snapshots before changes at line 2516 and returns detected changes at line 2567.
return collectProviderRowChanges(before, getProviderRowSnapshot(currentBody));
How Notifications Work
Notification creation starts at Today.cshtml line 2492:
notifyProviderRowChanges(changes)
It creates messages for new rows and status changes.
- Appointment added: Customer Name
- Walk-in added: Customer Name
- Appointment updated: Customer Name (Arrived)
- Walk-in updated: Customer Name (InService)
Full table sync triggers notifications at line 2603. Walk-in partial refresh triggers notifications at line 3482.
Why User Actions Do Not Spam Notifications
Normal button actions call queueLiveSync() without true. Only the 30-second external refresh calls queueLiveSync(true).
That means notifications are intended for external changes detected by polling, not every local button action.
Why We Fetch A Full Snapshot Instead Of One Row
The client does not know what another application changed. It could be an insert, status change, transfer, cancellation, meeting info update, or a row leaving the current date range.

The current MVC/Razor design already knows how to render correct row HTML, permissions, button attributes, locked state, and meeting data. Fetching the server-rendered snapshot avoids duplicating that row rendering logic in JavaScript.
The network fetch can be a full page/table snapshot, but the visible DOM update is row-level.
Future Improvement
A more optimized design would add an endpoint like:
GET /Provider/Changes?since=lastRefreshTime

That endpoint could return added/updated/removed row data only. Then the client would not need to fetch the full rendered HTML snapshot. The current implementation favors safety and reuse of existing Razor rendering.

Operational Checklist
- Open Provider Today.
- Insert a walk-in or appointment from the other app.
- Wait up to 30 seconds.
- Confirm the row appears without manual browser refresh.
- Confirm notification count increments.
- Open notification panel and confirm the message.
- Confirm action buttons are correctly enabled/disabled.
- Click Info/Meeting and expandable text to confirm delegated handlers still work.
